boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Pennsylvania
boards.description: Late-evening food and snack stops on campus and in nearby University City, using current public hours or Penn Dining’s late-night designation.

cards.title: Starbucks at 1920 Commons
cards.subtitle: 3800 Locust Walk, on campus
cards.notes: Use the downstairs 1920 Commons location for coffee, tea, pastries, or a snack; confirm the weekly schedule before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A Penn Dining location explicitly designated for late-night service.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Dining lists this Starbucks as a “Late Night” retail location and says it serves from early morning to late night.
cards.source_title: Starbucks | Penn Dining
cards.access_notes: Penn Dining currently labels it “Late Night”; weekly schedules can vary and should be checked through the linked schedule.

cards.title: Gourmet Grocer
cards.subtitle: 1920 Commons, 3800 Locust Walk
cards.notes: Pick up prepared food, snacks, essentials, or produce inside 1920 Commons, then check the current weekly schedule for that night.
cards.short_summary: A campus market identified by Penn Dining as a late-night option.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Dining labels Gourmet Grocer “Late Night” and describes it as open from early to late.
cards.source_title: Gourmet Grocer | Penn Dining
cards.access_notes: Penn Dining currently designates it “Late Night”; consult its linked weekly schedule because operating times can change.

cards.title: 1920 Commons
cards.subtitle: 3800 Locust Walk, west of the 38th Street Bridge
cards.notes: Head to the large dining café for an evening meal; check the current meal-period schedule, especially during breaks and summer.
cards.short_summary: Penn’s large Locust Walk dining café is described as serving from early to late.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Dining states that 1920 Commons is the largest café on campus and serves from early to late.
cards.source_title: Locations, Hours & Menus | Penn Dining
cards.access_notes: Penn Dining describes service as early to late; use the page’s weekly-schedule link to verify the date-specific closing time.

cards.title: Domino's on Chestnut Street
cards.subtitle: 4438 Chestnut Street, West Philadelphia
cards.notes: Use carryout or delivery from the West Philadelphia store when you need a food option after most nearby counters have closed.
cards.short_summary: A nearby pizza location whose official listing shows service until 2 a.m. today.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino’s official location page for 4438 Chestnut Street lists the store as open today until 2:00 a.m.
cards.source_title: Domino's Pizza at 4438 Chestnut Street
cards.access_notes: Official location page currently shows “Open Today Until 2:00 AM”; hours vary by day, so recheck before ordering.

cards.title: Greek Lady
cards.subtitle: University City
cards.notes: Choose a sit-down or takeout meal from the University City restaurant when an 11 p.m. closing fits your evening plans.
cards.short_summary: A University City restaurant with official daily hours through 11 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Greek Lady’s official site says it is in University City and open daily from 9:30 a.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.source_title: Greek Lady
cards.access_notes: Official site currently lists daily hours of 9:30 a.m.–11 p.m.; check before travel for exceptions.

cards.title: Renata's Kitchen
cards.subtitle: 3940 Baltimore Avenue, University City
cards.notes: Plan a dinner stop at the Baltimore Avenue restaurant Tuesday through Saturday, allowing time to arrive before the listed 11 p.m. close.
cards.short_summary: A University City restaurant whose official site lists 11 p.m. closing on Tuesday–Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Renata’s Kitchen lists its address as 3940 Baltimore Avenue and hours Tuesday–Saturday from 10 a.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.source_title: Renata's Kitchen
cards.access_notes: Official site currently lists Tuesday–Saturday service until 11 p.m.; it is closed Mondays and closes earlier Sunday.

cards.title: Landmark Americana University City
cards.subtitle: 3333 Market Street, University City
cards.notes: Use the food menu, not the bar program: the official site lists late-night kitchen service on every day of the week.
cards.short_summary: A Market Street restaurant with a separately listed late-night food schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: Landmark Americana’s University City page lists kitchen hours until 11 p.m. Sunday–Wednesday and midnight Thursday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Landmark Americana University City — Contact and Hours
cards.access_notes: Official page currently lists late-night kitchen service: until 11 p.m. Sun–Wed and midnight Thu–Sat; food service ends before venue closing.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies
cards.subtitle: Philadelphia-founded late-night bakery
cards.notes: Use the official store finder to select a nearby location and verify its night’s hours before placing a cookie or ice-cream order.
cards.short_summary: A late-night bakery brand founded in a University of Pennsylvania dorm room.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies states that the company was founded in a University of Pennsylvania dorm room and describes itself as serving warm cookies late into the night.
cards.source_title: Insomnia Cookies newsroom announcement
cards.access_notes: The official source establishes late-night service generally; verify the chosen Philadelphia store’s current hours in the official store finder.

cards.title: CO-OP Restaurant & Bar
cards.subtitle: 33rd and Chestnut Streets, University City
cards.notes: Make it an early-evening-to-late-evening meal stop inside The Study at University City; consult the restaurant’s current hours page before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A restaurant located at the 33rd-and-Chestnut edge of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: CO-OP’s official page places the restaurant in University City at the corner of 33rd and Chestnut Streets, inside The Study hotel.
cards.source_title: CO-OP Restaurant & Bar — Hours & Location
cards.access_notes: Use the official hours-and-location page to confirm same-day late service; it is a restaurant open to under-21 diners.

cards.title: Hill House Dining Cafe
cards.subtitle: 3333 Walnut Street, Hill College House
cards.notes: Use Hill’s food-hall-style dining café for an evening meal on the east side of campus; verify the evening meal period first.
cards.short_summary: A large east-campus dining café with seating around Hill’s atrium.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Dining identifies Hill House as the largest dining café on the east side of campus at the corner of 34th and Walnut Streets.
cards.source_title: Locations, Hours & Menus | Penn Dining
cards.access_notes: Penn Dining’s current location listing shows meal periods and links to the weekly schedule; evening availability varies by academic calendar.

warnings: Several Penn Dining locations provide a late-night designation or “early to late” description rather than a fixed daily closing time; check the linked weekly schedule before going.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten distinct Penn spaces for collaborative work, low-key breaks, cultural connection, performances, and campus gatherings.

cards.title: Weigle Information Commons
cards.subtitle: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center, first floor
cards.notes: Bring a group project here for reservable rooms, study booths, media tools, and collaborative workspaces; check library access and room availability first.
cards.short_summary: A technology-rich library commons built around collaborative study and media work.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries describes WIC as offering collaborative study spaces, technology-rich classrooms, equipment, and group study rooms and booths.
cards.source_title: Weigle Information Commons | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located at 3420 Walnut Street; Penn Libraries lists current building hours and room booking information.

cards.title: Goldstein Undergraduate Study Center
cards.subtitle: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center, ground floor
cards.notes: Use this library study center as a dependable starting point, then pair it with a reserved group room or quieter Rosengarten area nearby.
cards.short_summary: A named undergraduate study area inside Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists the Goldstein Undergraduate Study Center among the ground-floor student-centered spaces in Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center.
cards.source_title: Floor Plans: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center Ground Floor
cards.access_notes: Located in Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center at 3420 Walnut Street; follow current library access and hours.

cards.title: Rosengarten Quiet Study Area
cards.subtitle: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center, ground floor
cards.notes: Choose this named quiet area when you need solo concentration; keep calls and group discussion for the nearby collaborative rooms instead.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet-study option on Van Pelt’s ground floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries identifies the Rosengarten Quiet Study Area as part of the ground floor’s quiet and collaborative study environments.
cards.source_title: Floor Plans: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center Ground Floor
cards.access_notes: Located in Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center; observe current library policies and building hours.

cards.title: Education Commons
cards.subtitle: George A. Weiss Pavilion, Franklin Field mezzanine
cards.notes: Reserve a small group room when you need a screen and whiteboard, or use the commons’ flexible seating for a focused collaborative session.
cards.short_summary: A Franklin Field library commons with reservable, technology-equipped group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists Education Commons small group rooms with screens, computers, whiteboards, and seating for four or five people.
cards.source_title: Education Commons Small Group Study Rooms | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: Rooms 228–231 are on the mezzanine of the George A. Weiss Pavilion; reservation is required for these rooms.

cards.entity_name: The Game Room at the Student Union @ Houston Hall
cards.title: Houston Hall Game Room
cards.subtitle: Student Union @ Houston Hall, first floor
cards.notes: Meet friends for ping-pong, air hockey, foosball, arcade games, or a casual break between classes; confirm building access before heading over.
cards.short_summary: An open first-floor lounge for games, television, and social events.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn’s Student Union page says the Game Room is an open lounge with air hockey, ping-pong, Skeeball, foosball, arcade games, and a Smash Brothers corner.
cards.source_title: Student Union | University Life Space & Events
cards.access_notes: Located on Houston Hall’s first floor; the university posts current Houston Hall operating hours.

cards.entity_name: The Reading Room at the Student Union @ Houston Hall
cards.title: Houston Hall Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Student Union @ Houston Hall, first floor
cards.notes: Set up at a study table for solo work or meet a small group in the lounge seating; keep the space usable for others sharing it.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor Houston Hall room combining lounge furniture with study tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn describes the Reading Room as a first-floor Houston Hall space with lounge furniture and study tables for individual work or group meetups.
cards.source_title: Student Union | University Life Space & Events
cards.access_notes: Located on Houston Hall’s first floor; verify current Student Union operating hours.

cards.title: Silfen Study Center
cards.subtitle: Williams Hall, across the quad from Houston Hall
cards.notes: Bring your laptop for table outlets and printing, and use the nearby café separately if you want a break without leaving the study area.
cards.short_summary: A Williams Hall study space with charging outlets and self-service printing.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn’s Student Union page says Silfen Study Center has table outlets for laptops and phones plus a self-service printer.
cards.source_title: Student Union | University Life Space & Events
cards.access_notes: Located in Williams Hall near Williams Café; access follows current building policies.

cards.entity_name: The Arts, Research, and Culture House (ARCH)
cards.title: The ARCH
cards.subtitle: 3601 Locust Walk
cards.notes: Stop in for a campus resource, cultural-center program, performance-related activity, or a lounge study break; respect spaces reserved for programs and groups.
cards.short_summary: A restored Locust Walk landmark housing cultural centers, academic programs, lounges, and reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn identifies the ARCH as home to La Casa Latina, Makuu, and PAACH, with common areas and reservable rooms.
cards.source_title: The Arts, Research, and Culture House (ARCH) | University Life Space & Events
cards.access_notes: Address: 3601 Locust Walk. Access and room use may depend on campus operations or reservations.

cards.title: College Green
cards.subtitle: Central campus, between College Hall and Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center
cards.notes: Use the lawn or its edges for a daytime reset, an outdoor class, or a campus gathering; leave event setups and reserved areas to their organizers.
cards.short_summary: A central campus commons designed for both large events and smaller outdoor use.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn describes College Green as an iconic central commons and names reservable spaces there for concerts and public-speaking events.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Spaces | University Life Space & Events
cards.access_notes: The space includes reservable areas; follow Penn’s outdoor-space policies and avoid disrupting scheduled events.

cards.title: Covenant on Locust Walk
cards.subtitle: Locust Walk at 39th Street
cards.notes: Pause beneath or beside this large red landmark while walking the corridor, then use the university’s interpretation to connect the sculpture to its campus setting.
cards.short_summary: Alexander Lieberman’s 45-foot painted-steel Locust Walk landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Facilities identifies Covenant as a 1975 Alexander Lieberman sculpture of steel tubes, about 45 feet high, and a Locust Walk campus landmark.
cards.source_title: Discover Penn | University of Pennsylvania Facilities and Real Estate Services
cards.access_notes: Located at Locust Walk and 39th Street; view from the pedestrian corridor and do not climb on the artwork.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten current or scheduled Penn-area cultural activities whose supporting pages state that participation or admission is free.

cards.title: See contemporary art at the ICA
cards.subtitle: 118 South 36th Street
cards.notes: Bring a friend to browse the galleries, then pause over one work and compare what each of you noticed before moving on.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission contemporary-art stop on Penn’s campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn identifies the Institute of Contemporary Art as free for all to engage with contemporary art.
cards.source_title: Penn Resources & Facilities Open to the Public
cards.access_notes: Penn’s public-resources page states that the ICA is free for all; check the ICA calendar before visiting.

cards.entity_name: To Secure These Rights: 150 Years of Women at Penn
cards.title: Explore 150 years of women at Penn
cards.subtitle: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center, first floor · Aug. 31–Dec. 11, 2026
cards.notes: Walk the display together and pick one photograph, document, or story to discuss on the way out of Van Pelt.
cards.short_summary: A public library exhibition on women’s history at Penn.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries says this exhibition is free and open to the public from August 31 through December 11, 2026.
cards.source_title: To Secure These Rights: 150 Years of Women at Penn
cards.access_notes: Visitors outside Penn need a current government- or school-issued photo ID for library access.

cards.title: Print a Declaration at Common Press
cards.subtitle: Fisher Fine Arts Library, Lower Level · through Dec. 18, 2026
cards.notes: Reserve a slot with a small group and take turns at the handpress while learning how the historic text was set in type.
cards.short_summary: A reservation-based public letterpress activity at Fisher.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists this Common Press opportunity among programs free of charge and open to all.
cards.source_title: Common Press
cards.access_notes: Reserve ahead; the page says Common Press is by appointment except during monthly open studios, and visitors should review access guidelines.

cards.title: Hear the campus-landscape book launch
cards.subtitle: Kleinman Energy Forum, Fisher Fine Arts Library · Sept. 10, 2026
cards.notes: Register with a classmate and listen for one campus landscape detail you want to find on a later walk.
cards.short_summary: A public conversation about Penn’s campus landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: Weitzman lists the Penn’s Sylvania book launch as free and open to the public with advance registration.
cards.source_title: Penn’s Sylvania Book Launch
cards.access_notes: Advance registration is required; the event is scheduled for 6:30 p.m. on September 10, 2026.

cards.title: Catch Catherine Telford-Keogh’s artist talk
cards.subtitle: Institute of Contemporary Art · Oct. 22, 2026
cards.notes: Meet up before the talk, then use the walk back across campus to trade one question prompted by the presentation.
cards.short_summary: A free public visiting-artist lecture at the ICA.
cards.evidence_claim: Weitzman describes Catherine Telford-Keogh’s October 22, 2026 lecture at the ICA as free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Catherine Telford-Keogh
cards.access_notes: The lecture is scheduled for 6 p.m.; the event page says registration information is forthcoming.

cards.entity_name: Anarchitecture After Everything: A Trans Manifesto
cards.title: Join the Anarchitecture book talk
cards.subtitle: Wolf Humanities Center location to be determined · Oct. 28, 2026
cards.notes: Go with someone curious about art or design, and stay for the Q&A after Jack Halberstam’s illustrated book talk.
cards.short_summary: A free public humanities talk with a Q&A.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wolf Humanities Center lists this October 28, 2026 book talk as free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Anarchitecture After Everything: A Trans Manifesto
cards.access_notes: Scheduled 5:30–7 p.m.; the Wolf Humanities Center lists the location as to be determined.

cards.title: Attend Rachel Kolb’s ASL and English forum
cards.subtitle: Wolf Humanities Center location to be determined · Nov. 11, 2026
cards.notes: Plan to arrive with a friend and stay for the discussion on communication, language, and lived experience after the talk.
cards.short_summary: A public forum presented in ASL with ASL/English interpretation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wolf Humanities Center says Rachel Kolb’s November 11, 2026 forum is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: The Practice of Articulation
cards.access_notes: Scheduled 5:30–7:30 p.m.; registration and the final location are still forthcoming.

cards.entity_name: Common Press Workshops and Open Studios
cards.title: Try a free Common Press workshop
cards.subtitle: Common Press, Fisher Fine Arts Library
cards.notes: Watch the events calendar, reserve an eligible session, and make something together rather than just passing through the library.
cards.short_summary: Free public printmaking opportunities, with registration details on the calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries states that Common Press opportunities are free of charge and open to all.
cards.source_title: Common Press
cards.access_notes: Check the event calendar and access guidelines; the studio is by appointment except for monthly open studio sessions.

cards.entity_name: Weitzman School Fine Arts Lecture Series
cards.title: Make a plan for a free visiting-artist lecture
cards.subtitle: Usually Institute of Contemporary Art, 118 South 36th Street
cards.notes: Choose a listed speaker with friends, arrive a few minutes early, and use the conversation afterward to unpack one idea from the lecture.
cards.short_summary: A public lecture series featuring artists, activists, writers, and other guests.
cards.evidence_claim: Weitzman states that all lectures in its Fine Arts Visiting Artist Lecture Series are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Visiting Artists
cards.access_notes: Confirm the speaker’s venue and time on the series page; the page notes that some lectures may be held outside the ICA.

cards.entity_name: Penn Libraries Public Events and Exhibitions
cards.title: Build a no-cost library culture night
cards.subtitle: Penn Libraries locations across campus
cards.notes: Pick an event or exhibition marked public, pair it with a stroll through the library displays, and check access details before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A rotating calendar of public library events, performances, workshops, and exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries says many of its events and exhibitions are open to the public and lists free workshops in its programming.
cards.source_title: Events | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: Select a listing explicitly marked free and open to the public; individual event pages provide registration and access requirements.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Penn Libraries study environments spanning quiet desks, reservable group rooms, booths, and technology-equipped spaces.

cards.title: Rosengarten Quiet Study Area
cards.subtitle: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center, ground floor
cards.notes: Set up at one of 24 desks with power sockets when you want a designated quiet-study setting; use the library floor plan to orient yourself.
cards.short_summary: A ground-floor quiet area with desks and power.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists 24 seats and photographs desks with power sockets in this ground-floor Van Pelt-Dietrich quiet-study area.
cards.source_title: Rosengarten Quiet Study Area | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on the Van Pelt-Dietrich ground floor; library hours apply. The page documents accessible routes and nearby accessible restrooms.

cards.title: Brownlee Group Study Suite
cards.subtitle: G101.2 and G101.3, Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center
cards.notes: Reserve a four-seat room for a small working session, and use the in-room whiteboard to sketch a plan or divide up a problem set.
cards.short_summary: Two reservable, four-seat ground-floor rooms with whiteboards.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries identifies Brownlee as rooms G101.2 and G101.3, each seating four and equipped with a whiteboard.
cards.source_title: Brownlee Group Study Suite | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: Ground-floor Van Pelt-Dietrich rooms; reserve a room through Penn Libraries. The page notes accessible circulation and nearby accessible restrooms.

cards.title: Stovall/Dickey Group Study Room
cards.subtitle: G101.1, Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center
cards.notes: Book this four-seat room for a focused meeting and put the chalkboard to work for timelines, equations, or a shared outline.
cards.short_summary: A reservable four-seat room with a chalkboard.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists the Stovall/Dickey room at G101.1 with four seats, a chalkboard, and a room-reservation link.
cards.source_title: Stovall/Dickey Group Study Room | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reserve through Penn Libraries; food is not permitted and covered drinks are permitted. Accessible circulation details are listed on the page.

cards.title: Weigle Group Study Suite
cards.subtitle: Rooms 403 and 404, Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center
cards.notes: Reserve one of these sixth-floor-scale group rooms—actually on the fourth floor—and use its chalkboard when your work benefits from a shared surface.
cards.short_summary: Two fourth-floor rooms for groups of six, each with a chalkboard.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists rooms 403 and 404 on Van Pelt-Dietrich's fourth floor, with six seats per room and a chalkboard.
cards.source_title: Weigle Group Study Suite | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reserve a room through Penn Libraries. The page documents fourth-floor location, accessible circulation, and nearby accessible restrooms.

cards.title: WIC Group Study Rooms 117–120
cards.subtitle: Weigle Information Commons, Van Pelt-Dietrich first floor
cards.notes: Use a reservable room for a group of four to six when an iMac, articulated monitor, whiteboard, or video-conference camera supports the task.
cards.short_summary: Four technology-equipped, reservable WIC group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists rooms 117–120 in WIC with seating for four to six, iMacs, articulated monitors, whiteboards, and cameras.
cards.source_title: WIC Group Study Rooms 117 - 120 | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: First-floor WIC rooms; reserve through Penn Libraries. Non-aromatic food and drink are allowed, and accessibility information is provided.

cards.entity_name: Study Booths in the Weigle Information Commons
cards.title: Study Booths in the Weigle Information Commons
cards.subtitle: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center, first floor west
cards.notes: Reserve a booth when six people need a contained setup with a computer workstation; check the room-or-booth reservation tool before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Reservable WIC booths with computer workstations and six seats each.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists 12 WIC study and consultation booths, each seating six and equipped with a computer workstation, iMac, and PC desktop.
cards.source_title: Study booths in the Weigle Information Commons | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: First-floor-west WIC; use the Penn Libraries reservation link. Non-aromatic food and drink are allowed in this area.

cards.entity_name: Education Commons Small Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Education Commons Small Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Rooms 228–231, Education Commons at Franklin Field
cards.notes: Reserve one of these four- or five-seat rooms when a shared screen, desktop computer, and whiteboard will keep a small project moving.
cards.short_summary: Four compact Education Commons rooms with screens, PCs, and whiteboards.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists rooms 228–231 with four or five seats, a 46-inch screen, integrated computer system, PC desktop, and whiteboard.
cards.source_title: Education Commons Small Group Study Rooms | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: On the mezzanine of George A. Weiss Pavilion in Franklin Field; reserve through Penn Libraries. Accessible bathroom information is listed.

cards.entity_name: Education Commons Group Study Rooms for 10
cards.title: Education Commons Group Study Rooms for 10
cards.subtitle: Rooms 225, 226, and 235, Education Commons
cards.notes: Plan a larger working session here when a presentation screen, integrated computer system, desktop PC, and whiteboard suit the agenda.
cards.short_summary: Three reservable Education Commons rooms built for groups of ten.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists rooms 225, 226, and 235 with ten seats per room, an 80-inch screen, integrated computer system, PC desktop, and whiteboard.
cards.source_title: Education Commons Group Study Rooms for 10 | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reserve through Penn Libraries; the page provides accessible-entry and accessible-bathroom information for Education Commons.

cards.entity_name: Holman Biotech Commons 6-Seat Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Holman Biotech Commons 6-Seat Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Johnson Pavilion and Stemmler Hall, main level
cards.notes: Reserve a six-seat room for a working group, especially if adjustable office chairs and a dedicated table fit the way your team studies.
cards.short_summary: Reservable main-level group rooms with a table, computer, and six office chairs.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists group rooms 1, 4, 8, 10–13, 15, 19, and 20 with six seats; each contains a table, six office chairs, and a computer.
cards.source_title: Holman Biotech Commons: 6-seat group study rooms | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: Main level of Johnson Pavilion and Stemmler Hall; reserve through Penn Libraries. Food is not permitted; covered drinks are permitted.

cards.title: Holman Biotech Commons Study Alcoves
cards.subtitle: Johnson Pavilion, Holman Biotech Commons main level
cards.notes: Choose an alcove when lounge seating and two tables fit your session; keep food out and bring only a covered beverage if needed.
cards.short_summary: Three named alcoves pairing tables with lounge seats.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists the Gliklich, Polan, and Crowley Family Study Alcoves in Johnson Pavilion, with two tables and four lounge seats per alcove.
cards.source_title: Holman Biotech Commons: Study Alcoves | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on Holman Biotech Commons' main level. Food is not permitted; beverages must be covered. The page lists accessible entry and restroom details.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten campus-adjacent corridors, each anchored by a named destination with a directly sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: South Street: Penn Museum
cards.subtitle: South Street corridor at 33rd Street
cards.notes: Walk South Street to the museum entrance and plan around its current galleries or public programs; confirm admission options before you go.
cards.short_summary: A named museum destination at South and 33rd Streets.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn identifies the Penn Museum at 3260 South Street, at the intersection of South and S. 33rd Streets.
cards.source_title: Directions to the Department | Department of Anthropology
cards.access_notes: Museum hours and admission conditions can vary; check the museum before visiting.

cards.title: Walnut Street: World Cafe Live
cards.subtitle: Walnut Street corridor at 31st Street
cards.notes: Use the venue calendar to choose an all-ages performance or community program, then approach from Walnut Street at the listed address.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit live-music venue on Walnut Street.
cards.evidence_claim: World Cafe Live describes itself as a nonprofit independent venue for live music, education, and community engagement at 3025 Walnut Street.
cards.source_title: About | World Cafe Live
cards.access_notes: Event availability, ticketing, and age policies vary by program; consult the venue calendar.

cards.title: 36th Street: ICA Philadelphia
cards.subtitle: South 36th Street corridor near Sansom Street
cards.notes: Enter at 118 South 36th Street and browse the exhibitions on view; the ICA’s official site states that admission is always free.
cards.short_summary: Free contemporary-art exhibitions on South 36th Street.
cards.evidence_claim: ICA Philadelphia is at 118 S. 36th Street and states that it is always free for all visitors.
cards.source_title: ICA Philadelphia
cards.access_notes: ICA lists public hours Wednesday through Sunday; review current exhibition and visit information before heading over.

cards.title: 40th Street: The Rotunda
cards.subtitle: Walnut Street corridor at 40th Street
cards.notes: Check the public calendar for a film, music, poetry, theater, class, or lecture, then follow the path from Walnut Street to the entrance.
cards.short_summary: An all-ages public arts venue just off Walnut Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rotunda at 4014 Walnut Street books public arts and culture events including music, film, dance, theater, poetry, classes, and lectures; all ages are admitted.
cards.source_title: The Rotunda | Contact
cards.access_notes: Programs and any ticket requirements vary; verify the event listing before visiting.

cards.title: Woodland Avenue: The Woodlands
cards.subtitle: Woodland Avenue corridor at 40th Street
cards.notes: Enter from Woodland Avenue for a daylight walk through the historic landscape; leave by the gates before they close at dusk.
cards.short_summary: A historic landscape and cemetery across from the 40th Street Trolley Portal.
cards.evidence_claim: The Woodlands is at 4000 Woodland Avenue, directly across from the 40th Street Trolley Portal, and its gates are open from dawn until dusk.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | The Woodlands
cards.access_notes: Respect that this is an active cemetery; self-guided visits are during daylight gate hours.

cards.title: 30th Street: Cira Green
cards.subtitle: South 30th Street corridor at Chestnut Street
cards.notes: Take the elevator from the Cira Centre South garage and use the elevated park as a daylight outdoor stop; check its posted access details first.
cards.short_summary: An elevated park above the Cira Centre South garage.
cards.evidence_claim: Cira Green’s official FAQ identifies it as an elevated park in University City and directs visitors to the Cira Centre South Garage at 129 S. 30th Street.
cards.source_title: Cira Green Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Review current access and event information before visiting.

cards.title: Baltimore Avenue: Clark Park
cards.subtitle: Baltimore Avenue corridor at 43rd Street
cards.notes: Use the park’s paths, playground, court, or scheduled community market as a daytime stop along Baltimore Avenue.
cards.short_summary: A nine-acre public park with recreation amenities and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: Philadelphia Parks & Recreation describes Clark Park as a nine-acre West Philadelphia park with historic features, a basketball court, playground, community events, and a year-round farmers market.
cards.source_title: Clark Park Engagement Assistant position description
cards.access_notes: Market schedules and recreational programming vary; check current event information.

cards.title: Baltimore Avenue: Trolley Portal Gardens
cards.subtitle: Baltimore Avenue corridor at 40th Street
cards.notes: Pause at the 40th Street Trolley Portal and look for the seasonal, all-ages pop-ups that University City District programs there.
cards.short_summary: A garden public space at the 40th Street trolley portal.
cards.evidence_claim: University City District identifies Trolley Portal Gardens at 40th Street and Baltimore Avenue and programs free, family-friendly events there.
cards.source_title: Trolley Portal Gardens Events | University City District
cards.access_notes: The listed free pop-ups are seasonal; consult the current schedule for dates and times.

cards.title: Cuthbert Street: The Lawn
cards.subtitle: Cuthbert Street corridor at 37th Street
cards.notes: Use the seating and green space at 37th and Cuthbert, or time your stop for the listed food-truck, music, movie, fitness, or craft programming.
cards.short_summary: A one-acre public lawn with seating and recurring programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lawn at uCity Square is a public space at 37th and Cuthbert Streets with seating, green areas, and events including music, movies, fitness classes, crafts, and food trucks.
cards.source_title: The Lawn | uCity Square
cards.access_notes: Individual events and food vendors may have their own costs and schedules.

cards.title: Market Street: Drexel Square
cards.subtitle: Market Street corridor at 30th Street
cards.notes: Walk to the 30th and Market corner for a green outdoor pause beside the station; pair it with a transit arrival or departure.
cards.short_summary: A 1.3-acre community park across from 30th Street Station.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel University identifies Drexel Square as a 1.3-acre community park at the corner of 30th and Market Streets, directly across from 30th Street Station.
cards.source_title: Drexel and Brandywine Open Drexel Square
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor public park; check local conditions or scheduled events before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Penn traditions spanning first-year welcome, class milestones, campus ritual, and athletic spirit.

cards.title: Toss toast at Franklin Field
cards.subtitle: Penn football tradition
cards.notes: At home football games, listen for “Here’s a toast to dear old Penn,” then observe the coordinated bread toss from the stands.
cards.short_summary: A football-game ritual tied to Penn’s unofficial alma mater.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn’s Office of Student Affairs documents toast throwing after the third quarter of football games, timed to the lyric “Here’s a toast to dear old Penn.”
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions | Office of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Occurs at Penn home football games; follow current stadium guidance and event policies.

cards.title: Mark junior-to-senior year on Hey Day
cards.subtitle: Annual class-rank celebration
cards.notes: Watch for the third-year class’s red shirts, mock skimmer hats, and canes as Penn marks its move to fourth-year status.
cards.short_summary: Penn’s annual rising-senior ceremony, begun in 1916.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Today reports that Hey Day began in 1916 and uses hats, canes, and a class celebration to symbolize third-years’ rise to fourth-year rank.
cards.source_title: Class of 2027 sparks traditional spirit on Hey Day | Penn Today
cards.access_notes: For Penn third-year students; date and program are announced annually.

cards.title: Find a graduating class’s Ivy Stone
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide class memorial tradition
cards.notes: Look closely at College Hall, Penn Commons, and other campus locations for engraved stones that record graduating classes and Ivy Day.
cards.short_summary: Each graduating class leaves a physical campus marker.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn states that each graduating class has contributed an Ivy Stone to campus since 1873.
cards.source_title: Ivy Stones 1873–2025 | Office of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Stones are installed around campus; view them from publicly accessible outdoor areas.

cards.title: See the Ivy Day Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Graduating fourth-year recognition
cards.notes: Follow the annual Ivy Day coverage to see the graduating class unveil its Ivy Stone and recognize student leadership and service.
cards.short_summary: A 150-year-plus graduating-class observance.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Today says the annual Ivy Day celebration includes unveiling a class Ivy Stone and an awards ceremony for graduating fourth-year students.
cards.source_title: Class of 2026 Ivy Day Ceremony | Penn Today
cards.access_notes: Held during Alumni Weekend; current ceremony details are announced by Penn.

cards.title: Recognize the Spoon, Bowl, Cane, and Spade
cards.subtitle: Ivy Day’s historic class honors
cards.notes: At Ivy Day, notice the named Senior Honor Awards—Spoon, Bowl, Cane, and Spade—which link today’s recipients to Penn history.
cards.short_summary: Historic awards remain part of the Ivy Day tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Today identifies the Bowl, Spade, Cane, and Spoon as Senior Honor Awards presented at the Ivy Day Ceremony.
cards.source_title: Class of 2026 Ivy Day Ceremony | Penn Today
cards.access_notes: Recipients and ceremony details vary by graduating class.

cards.title: Raise a lantern at U-Night
cards.subtitle: Second-year class milestone
cards.notes: Second-year students gather near sunset and join the lantern exercise that marks their transition toward junior year at Penn.
cards.short_summary: A newer class tradition centered on light and the halfway point.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Today reports that each second-year class has gathered since 2019 for U-Night, including a traditional lantern exercise.
cards.source_title: Penn’s Class of 2027 marks the midway at U-Night | Penn Today
cards.access_notes: For Penn second-year students; location and timing are announced annually.

cards.title: Hear the Econ Scream
cards.subtitle: Lower Quadrangle, before Microeconomics 001 midterm
cards.notes: If you are nearby at midnight before the first Microeconomics 001 midterm, expect the annual collective shout from the Junior Balcony.
cards.short_summary: A midnight stress-release ritual associated with Econ 001.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn’s Office of Student Affairs documents Econ Scream as a collective midnight shout on the Junior Balcony before the first Microeconomics 001 midterm.
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions | Office of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Timing follows the first Microeconomics 001 midterm; be considerate of nearby residents and campus rules.

cards.title: Track Penn’s Spring Fling
cards.subtitle: Annual spring campus tradition
cards.notes: Check Penn’s current program for Spring Fling activities, a campus tradition that began in 1973 and has often used the Quadrangle.
cards.short_summary: A long-running springtime Penn event with Quad roots.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn’s Office of Student Affairs states that students began the annual Spring Fling tradition in 1973 and that it has taken place in the Quadrangle in many years.
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions | Office of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Programming, access, and location vary by year; consult current Penn announcements.

cards.title: Enter Penn at Convocation
cards.subtitle: Franklin Field welcome ceremony
cards.notes: Incoming students process into Penn’s formal welcome ceremony, the opening milestone in a sequence that later includes Hey Day and Commencement.
cards.short_summary: A first-year ceremony with roots in Penn’s nineteenth century.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn’s Office of the University Secretary describes Convocation as Penn’s formal incoming-class welcome and dates its modern form to around 1894.
cards.source_title: Convocation | Office of the University Secretary
cards.access_notes: For the incoming class; Penn announces the current ceremony’s date and attendance information.

cards.title: Send off seniors at Final Toast
cards.subtitle: Hey Day’s senior-class counterpart
cards.notes: During Hey Day, the outgoing senior class gathers for its separate sendoff while the junior class is inaugurated into its final undergraduate year.
cards.short_summary: A senior-to-alumni milestone held alongside Hey Day.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Today reports that Final Toast, first celebrated in 2009, celebrates the senior class and symbolically elevates participants to alumni status.
cards.source_title: Hey Day 2016 | Penn Today
cards.access_notes: Held in connection with Hey Day; participation details are announced through Penn Traditions.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Pennsylvania, Shared as Cards
boards.description: An under-21-safe first-weekend sequence that starts with campus orientation, adds a few low-pressure gathering places, and leaves room for museum and garden exploration.

cards.title: Start with a campus-length walk
cards.subtitle: Brick pedestrian thoroughfare at the heart of Penn
cards.notes: Walk the brick route between 40th and 34th streets to orient yourself, then use its crossings as landmarks for returning to residence or class buildings.
cards.short_summary: A simple first route through Penn’s central campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn identifies Locust Walk as a brick-lined pedestrian thoroughfare at the heart of the University of Pennsylvania campus.
cards.source_title: Philadelphia Campus | The Wharton School
cards.access_notes: Outdoor pedestrian route; follow posted campus conditions and crossings.

cards.title: Meet at the LOVE sculpture
cards.subtitle: Robert Indiana sculpture in Blanche Levy Park
cards.notes: Use the painted-aluminum sculpture as an easy daylight meeting point, then take a group photo before continuing across College Green.
cards.short_summary: A named campus artwork with a clear visual landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn lists Robert Indiana’s painted-aluminum LOVE sculpture at Blanche Levy Park and places it on the campus map.
cards.source_title: Love | University of Pennsylvania Facilities and Real Estate Services
cards.access_notes: Outdoor artwork in Blanche Levy Park; do not climb on the sculpture.

cards.title: Pause at Penn’s first West Philadelphia building
cards.subtitle: Historic building on College Green
cards.notes: Read the campus-history marker and take in the Victorian Gothic exterior from College Green; check in with reception if you need to enter.
cards.short_summary: A historic anchor for learning the campus layout.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn states that College Hall was the first building built on its current campus after the University moved from downtown Philadelphia.
cards.source_title: College Hall | University of Pennsylvania Facilities and Real Estate Services
cards.access_notes: Penn’s accessibility page says visitors should use the north entrance and check in with reception/security; accessible visitors can use the east-entrance intercom.

cards.title: Find the student union
cards.subtitle: Houston Hall, Penn’s historic student union
cards.notes: Stop by the student union to identify its gathering spaces and current programming, then choose a public event or simply use it as a regrouping point.
cards.short_summary: A campus hub for social, cultural, recreational, and educational activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn describes Houston Hall as the nation’s oldest operating student union and a place for students, faculty, staff, alumni, and guests to gather.
cards.source_title: University Life Space & Events
cards.access_notes: The posted student-union schedule lists 7:30 a.m.–11 p.m. Monday–Friday and 8 a.m.–11 p.m. Saturday–Sunday; confirm before going.

cards.title: Set a library rendezvous point
cards.subtitle: 3420 Walnut Street
cards.notes: Locate the main library early, review its current access guidance, and pick a nearby entrance as a dependable daytime regrouping point for your first weekend.
cards.short_summary: Penn’s central library is useful as both a study and navigation landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center at 3420 Walnut Street and provides current hours and visitor information.
cards.source_title: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: Penn Libraries posts current hours and separate access/visitor information; access policies can vary, so check before arrival.

cards.title: Check the ICA’s current exhibition
cards.subtitle: Penn contemporary-art museum
cards.notes: Look at the museum’s current exhibition information before you go, then make time for a quiet gallery visit with new friends during public operating hours.
cards.short_summary: A Penn cultural stop with PennCard admission access.
cards.evidence_claim: PennCard states that admission to the Institute of Contemporary Art is free with a valid PennCard.
cards.source_title: Where To Use PennCard | PennCard
cards.access_notes: Bring a valid PennCard; check the ICA directly for current exhibition and visitor hours.

cards.title: Spend an afternoon at Penn Museum
cards.subtitle: 3260 South Street
cards.notes: Choose a gallery or collection to explore together, leaving time to read object labels rather than trying to cover the entire museum in one visit.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum visit that can fit a relaxed weekend afternoon.
cards.evidence_claim: PennCard states that admission to the Penn Museum is free with a valid PennCard.
cards.source_title: Where To Use PennCard | PennCard
cards.access_notes: Bring a valid PennCard; verify current museum hours and gallery availability before visiting.

cards.title: Take a daylight break on Shoemaker Green
cards.subtitle: Public commons near Franklin Field and the Palestra
cards.notes: Use the tree-lined walkways and seating for a daylight pause, then look toward the surrounding athletic landmarks before heading back across campus.
cards.short_summary: A public campus commons designed for both groups and individual respite.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn describes Shoemaker Green as a public commons with open space, tree-lined walkways, and sitting areas.
cards.source_title: Shoemaker Green | University of Pennsylvania Facilities and Real Estate Services
cards.access_notes: Outdoor commons; follow any posted event reservations, facility rules, and weather guidance.

cards.title: Take the leafy route toward Kaskey Park
cards.subtitle: Walkway from 38th to 36th Street
cards.notes: Follow Hamilton Walk at an unhurried pace and make a daylight detour toward Kaskey Park’s pond area; stay on maintained paths and respect campus signage.
cards.short_summary: A tree-lined campus route with an adjacent landscaped park.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn identifies Hamilton Walk as a verdant walkway from 38th to 36th Street with more than 500 trees and numerous plant types.
cards.source_title: Discover Penn | University of Pennsylvania Facilities and Real Estate Services
cards.access_notes: Outdoor walkway; visit in daylight and observe posted park and campus rules.

cards.title: Plan a garden outing with your PennCard
cards.subtitle: 100 East Northwestern Avenue, Chestnut Hill
cards.notes: If your weekend allows for an off-campus outing, plan a daytime garden visit and check the arboretum’s entry procedures before leaving University City.
cards.short_summary: A Penn garden destination with admission covered for PennCard holders.
cards.evidence_claim: PennCard states that University of Pennsylvania students, faculty, and staff are admitted to Morris Arboretum free with a valid PennCard.
cards.source_title: Where To Use PennCard | PennCard
cards.access_notes: Bring a valid PennCard and check Morris Arboretum’s current hours, entry procedures, and transportation options before travel.
